summary: West Covina sits in the eastern San Gabriel Valley with the San Gabriel Mountains forming a dramatic northern wall — close enough that snowcapped peaks are visible from parking lots on clear winter mornings, yet the city itself occupies a broad, flat valley floor where 77°F average highs and 9.3 hours of daily sunshine make overcast days feel like a scheduling error. With roughly 110,000 people packed into 16 square miles, it registers denser than many realize, but the landscape reads as wide-laned commercial corridors and residential blocks rather than anything vertical — the Eastland Shopping Center and the Plaza at West Covina anchor big-box retail gravity, making this more of a drive-between-errands city than a stroll-to-dinner one. The median home price of $712,300 against a median household income of $98,570 produces a price-to-income ratio around 7.2, meaning purchasing requires either substantial savings or dual incomes even at the median. The I-10 and I-210 freeways make this largely a bedroom community feeding jobs westward toward downtown Los Angeles and the greater SGV healthcare and logistics sectors — employers within city limits skew toward retail, education, and medical offices rather than large corporate campuses. A 95.6% high school graduation rate across 26 schools is notably high for a city this size. At its core, West Covina offers mountain-adjacent suburbia with real purchasing friction — a place where the commute buys you square footage and sunshine, but not necessarily a short drive to work.
